title: Exponents and Logarithms
description: Laws of exponents, logarithms and their laws, change of base, and exponential models

notes.heading: Laws of Exponents
notes.body:
An exponent counts repeated multiplication, and the laws extend that idea to negative and fractional powers.

$$
a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}, \qquad \frac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}, \qquad (a^m)^n = a^{mn}
$$
$$a^0 = 1, \qquad a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^n}, \qquad a^{\frac1n} = \sqrt[n]{a}, \qquad a^{\frac{m}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{a^m}$$

💡 **Worked Example** — $\dfrac{2^7 \times 2^{-3}}{2^2} = 2^{7-3-2} = 2^{2} = 4$, and $27^{\frac23} = (\sqrt[3]{27})^2 = 3^2 = 9$.

📌 Work with one base wherever possible: converting $8$ to $2^3$ or $9$ to $3^2$ turns many equations into a single comparison of exponents.

illustration.alt: The index laws for exponents beside the matching laws for logarithms, and a graph of an exponential function with its logarithm drawn as the reflection that makes them inverses.
illustration.caption: A logarithm answers the question of what power the base is raised to, which is why each index law has a matching logarithm law.

notes.heading: Solving Equations by Matching Bases
notes.body:
If both sides of an equation can be written as powers of the same base, the exponents must be equal.

💡 **Worked Example** — Solve $3^{2x-1} = 27$.
$$3^{2x-1} = 3^3 \;\Longrightarrow\; 2x - 1 = 3 \;\Longrightarrow\; x = 2$$

📌 This method needs a common base. If there is none — for example $5^x = 12$ — you need logarithms instead.

⚠️ A common slip is writing $3^{2x-1} = 27$ as $2x - 1 = 27$: the exponent must be compared with the exponent, not with the value.

notes.heading: What a Logarithm Is
notes.body:
A **logarithm** answers the question *what power do I raise the base to?*

$$\log_a x = n \iff a^n = x \qquad (a > 0, \; a \neq 1, \; x > 0)$$

💡 **Worked Example** — $\log_2 32 = 5$ because $2^5 = 32$, and $\log_3 \frac19 = -2$ because $3^{-2} = \frac19$.

🔑 Two bases have their own notation:
• $\log x$ means $\log_{10} x$ — the **common** logarithm.
• $\ln x$ means $\log_e x$ — the **natural** logarithm, with $e \approx 2.718$.

📌 A logarithm of a negative number or of zero does not exist, because a positive base never gives a negative result.

notes.heading: Laws of Logarithms
notes.body:
Logarithms turn multiplication into addition, which is exactly why they are useful.

$$\log_a(xy) = \log_a x + \log_a y$$
$$\log_a\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) = \log_a x - \log_a y$$
$$\log_a(x^k) = k\log_a x$$

Also $\log_a a = 1$, $\log_a 1 = 0$, and $\log_a x = \dfrac{\log_b x}{\log_b a}$ — the **change of base** rule.

💡 **Worked Example** — Writing $\log_2 40$ in terms of $\log_2 5$:
$$\log_2 40 = \log_2(8 \times 5) = \log_2 8 + \log_2 5 = 3 + \log_2 5$$

⚠️ There is no rule for $\log_a(x + y)$ — only products, quotients and powers can be split.

notes.heading: Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equations
notes.body:
When the unknown is in the exponent and there is no common base, take logarithms of both sides.

💡 **Worked Example** — Solve $5^x = 12$.
$$x \log 5 = \log 12 \;\Longrightarrow\; x = \frac{\log 12}{\log 5} \approx 1.54$$

For an equation containing logarithms, combine them into a single logarithm first.

💡 **Worked Example** — Solve $\log_2 x + \log_2(x - 2) = 3$.
$$\log_2\big(x(x-2)\big) = 3 \;\Longrightarrow\; x(x-2) = 8 \;\Longrightarrow\; x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0$$
$$(x-4)(x+2) = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; x = 4 \text{ or } x = -2$$

⚠️ Substituting back, $x = -2$ is **rejected** because $\log_2(-2)$ does not exist. Always check your solutions in the original equation.

notes.heading: Exponential Models
notes.body:
Exponential models describe anything changing by a constant factor, and $e$ is the base that makes the calculus clean.

$$A = A_0 e^{kt}$$

Here $A_0$ is the initial amount, $k$ is the rate constant, and $t$ is time. If $k > 0$ the quantity grows; if $k < 0$ it decays.

💡 **Worked Example** — A population of 400 bacteria grows by 5% per hour. Using $A = 400(1.05)^t$, after 12 hours $A \approx 718$.

🔑 Doubling time and half-life come from solving $e^{kt} = 2$ or $e^{kt} = \frac12$, giving $t = \frac{\ln 2}{k}$ and $t = -\frac{\ln 2}{k}$ respectively.

📌 A percentage change per year is a multiplier like $1.05$; continuous growth uses $e^{kt}$. Both are exponential — read which one the question intends.

notes.heading: Common Errors and Exam Technique
notes.body:
**Checklist**
• Is there a common base? If yes, match exponents; if no, take logs.
• After solving a logarithmic equation, substitute back and reject invalid solutions.
• When using $\log$, remember $\log_a 1 = 0$ and $\log_a a = 1$.

⚠️ **Common mistakes**
• Writing $\log(x + y) = \log x + \log y$ — false.
• Dropping the base: $\log 12$ means $\log_{10} 12$, which is rarely what the question wants unless it says so.
• Losing a solution by dividing by $x$ or by a log term instead of factorising.
• Rounding too early: keep full accuracy until the final answer.

📌 Give answers to 3 significant figures unless the question specifies otherwise.

questions.explanation: Add the exponents on top and subtract the one below: $8 + (-2) - 4 = 2$, so the answer is $3^2 = 9$.
$\log_3 81$ asks for the power of 3 that gives 81, and $3^4 = 81$.
Any base raised to the power 0 gives 1, so $\ln 1 = 0$.
The quotient rule subtracts and the power rule brings the 3 down: $\log x^3 - \log y = 3\log x - \log y$.

questions.stem: A radioactive sample decays so that $A = 80e^{-0.04t}$ grams after $t$ years. Find its half-life to 3 significant figures.

questions.explanation: Combining gives $\log_2[x(x+6)] = 4$, so $x^2 + 6x = 16$ and $x^2 + 6x - 16 = 0$, i.e. $(x+8)(x-2)=0$. The root $x = -8$ is rejected because $\log_2(-8)$ does not exist, leaving $x = 2$.

questions.stem: If $\log_a 2 = p$ and $\log_a 5 = q$, express $\log_a 50$ in terms of $p$ and $q$.
The number of bacteria in a culture is modelled by $N = 500e^{0.18t}$ with $t$ in hours. How many hours until the population reaches 5000?
Given $3^{2x} - 10(3^x) + 9 = 0$, find the positive solution for $x$.
questions.explanation: Writing $y = 3^x$ gives $y^2 - 10y + 9 = 0$, so $(y-1)(y-9)=0$ and $y = 1$ or $y = 9$. Then $3^x = 1$ gives $x = 0$ and $3^x = 9$ gives $x = 2$, so the positive solution is $x = 2$.

questions.stem: Which statement is true for all $a > 0$, $a \neq 1$ and positive $x$, $y$?
questions.explanation: The quotient rule states $\log_a\frac{x}{y} = \log_a x - \log_a y$. The other three confuse the laws: sums cannot be split, the product rule is an addition, and the power rule brings the index down as a factor.
